newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end moderately higher,near peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end moderately higher,near peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures upticked further late to end busy trading moderately higher and near peaks.
March Treasury bond futures rose to the day's high at 111-16/32 during the last 10 minutes on what traders said was local shortcovering before Friday's December U.S. jobs report.

"It was the same old story: When the locals couldn't push them lower, they covered shorts," said one floor bank broker. "I don't think people were too long going into today, and I don't think people wanted to be short going into tomorrow. Who in their right mind would want to have a large position into unemployment?"

Nonfarm payrolls are forecast rising 192,000 from November's original 118,000 rise. The jobless rates is seen slipping to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent, average hourly earnings are expected to rise 0.2 percent, and the workweek is seen steady at 34.5 hours.
Some technicians had expected the contract might rebound from Tuesday's decline, and one had pegged the 111-16/32 level as a satisfactory retracement point.
Some noted the contract's ability to recover and settle back above old supports at 111-00 and 111-05/32, but the floor bank broker was unimpressed.
"It means nothing," she added. "It needs to settle above 18 (111-18/32) to be important."
Gains on Thursday in the dollar and US stocks plus erosion in crude oil and Commodity Research Bureau Index added lift.

Futures moved little on remarks by Federal Reserve governor Susan Phillips and Chicago Fed president Michael Moskow. Phillips said she saw some risks - specifically tight labor markets - to the price picture and that the Fed must stay on guard.
Moskow said the U.S. economy did well in 1996, and he predicted more of the same for the economy in 1997.

Some brokers said futures rose on signs of tame core wholesale-level inflation last month, when PPI rose 0.5 percent overall but firmed only 0.1 percent in the core rate versus forecasts for up 0.3 percent and 0.1 percent, respectively.

March T-bonds ended up 22/32 at 111-13/32 T-notes rose 12/32 to 108-20/32, muni-bonds added 16/32 to 115-03/32, T-bills rose two bps to 94.93, Eurodollars added one bp to 94.39. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
